correctness.rationale: Pinching into accepted/rejected blocks cannot increase trace distance. Each block contributes at least half the acceptance-probability gap by its trace, while for \(p\ge q\) the accepted block also satisfies \(\delta_P\ge pc-|p-q|/2\) by the triangle inequality. Adding the rejected-block contribution yields exactly \(\max\{|p-q|,pc\}\); swapping states handles \(q\ge p\). The three-outcome diagonal family has conditional distance \(c_*=\min(1,\tau/p)\) and input distance \(\max(p-q,pc_*)\le\tau\), proving sharpness. A fresh independent random-matrix check verified the inequality on 100 noncommuting instances. The relationship paragraph in RESULT.md contains one pre-existing unmatched LaTeX brace in its display of the weaker source bound; the theorem and proof are unaffected.
residual_risks: One non-substantive malformed brace appears only in a prior-work formula in RESULT.md.

final_claim: For two finite-dimensional states subjected to a common orthogonal-projector postselection with acceptance probabilities \(p,q>0\), if the input trace distance is \(\varepsilon\) and the conditional trace distance is \(c\), then \(\varepsilon\ge\max\{|p-q|,\max(p,q)c\}\). Hence an input budget \(\tau\) gives the sharp envelope \(c\le\min\{1,\tau/\max(p,q)\}\), attained for every feasible \(p,q,\tau\).
